references.text: Describes the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night that led Israel out of Egypt, the same divine guidance that Moses refers to.
The pillar of cloud that stood at the entrance of the tent when the Lord spoke with Moses face to face, parallel to the expression 'eye to eye'.
The cloud covered the tent of meeting and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle; the cloud and fire led Israel on their journeys.
A detailed description of how the cloud covered the tabernacle and turned into fire at night, and how it guided Israel's wanderings.
The Lord went before Israel in fire by night and in a cloud by day to show them the way.
Speaks of how no nation has a god so near as the Lord is to Israel, parallel to the Lord's presence 'in the midst' of the people.
Nehemiah reminds of the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night that led the people.
The psalm describes how God guided the people with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all through the night.
God spoke to them in the pillar of cloud, a reference to God's visible presence among the people.
The expression 'eye to eye' is used regarding seeing the Lord when he returns to Zion.
Paul refers to how the fathers were under the cloud, an allusion to God's guidance of Israel in the wilderness.
